subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A researcher is tracing the developmental origin of the formed elements of blood. She identifies a population of primitive cells in the bone marrow capable of giving rise to both myeloid and lymphoid progeny. She wants to determine which branch ultimately produces platelets.
question: From which stem cell lineage do megakaryocytes and platelets arise?
explanation_correct: The multipotent hematopoietic stem cell in bone marrow divides into two major branches: the myeloid stem cell and the lymphoid stem cell. The myeloid stem cell gives rise to the erythroid, megakaryocytic, granulocytic, and monocytic lineages. Megakaryocytes develop from the megakaryocytic branch and shed platelets into the circulation. Therefore platelets are of myeloid, not lymphoid, origin.

explanation_incorrect.A: The lymphoid stem cell produces B cells, T cells, and NK cells; it does not generate megakaryocytes or platelets.
explanation_incorrect.C: The erythroid progenitor gives rise to erythrocytes (red blood cells), not platelets.
explanation_incorrect.D: The monocytic progenitor produces monocytes and, in tissues, macrophages and dendritic cells.
explanation_incorrect.E: The granulocytic progenitor produces neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils.

educationalObjective: Platelets and megakaryocytes arise from the myeloid stem cell, whereas lymphocytes arise from the lymphoid stem cell.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 58-year-old man with multiple myeloma has a bone marrow biopsy showing a clonal proliferation of plasma cells that secrete monoclonal IgG. To understand the cell's normal lineage, the pathologist reviews its developmental origin.
question: Plasma cells are terminally differentiated cells derived from which of the following precursors?
explanation_correct: Plasma cells are terminally differentiated B lymphocytes that are specialized for high-rate antibody secretion. B cells belong to the lymphoid lineage, which also includes T cells and NK cells. After antigen stimulation, B cells can differentiate into memory B cells or antibody-secreting plasma cells. This is why plasma cell disorders such as multiple myeloma produce a monoclonal immunoglobulin.

explanation_incorrect.A: T-helper cells are lymphoid cells that provide help to B cells but do not themselves become antibody-secreting plasma cells.
explanation_incorrect.B: Monocytes are myeloid cells that mature into macrophages and dendritic cells in tissues, not plasma cells.
explanation_incorrect.C: Megakaryocytes are myeloid cells that produce platelets; they are not related to plasma cells.
explanation_incorrect.E: Neutrophils are myeloid granulocytes involved in acute inflammation and do not give rise to plasma cells.

educationalObjective: Plasma cells are antibody-secreting cells derived from B lymphocytes of the lymphoid lineage.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A laboratory scientist is studying a culture of bone marrow progenitor cells after adding a growth factor that selectively supports lymphoid differentiation. She wants to know which mature cell types should appear in the culture.
question: Which of the following sets of mature cells belongs to the lymphoid lineage?

options.text: B cells, T cells, and NK cells

explanation_correct: The lymphoid stem cell gives rise to B cells, T cells, and NK cells. B cells mature in bone marrow and can become plasma cells; T cells mature in the thymus and include helper and cytotoxic subsets. NK cells are innate lymphoid cells. None of these are myeloid-derived.

explanation_incorrect.B: Neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils are granulocytes derived from the myeloid stem cell through granulocytopoiesis.
explanation_incorrect.C: Erythrocytes and platelets are myeloid-derived, arising from the erythroid and megakaryocytic branches respectively.
explanation_incorrect.D: Monocytes and macrophages are myeloid cells produced by monocytopoiesis.
explanation_incorrect.E: Megakaryocytes and erythroblasts are both myeloid progenitors, giving rise to platelets and erythrocytes.

educationalObjective: The lymphoid lineage comprises B cells, T cells, and NK cells, all arising from the lymphoid stem cell.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 24-year-old man with a severe bacterial infection has a peripheral smear showing increased neutrophils along with band cells and metamyelocytes. His physician discusses that granulocytes and monocytes share a common stem cell origin.
question: Which stem cell gives rise to both granulocytes and monocytes?
explanation_correct: Granulocytopoiesis and monocytopoiesis both branch from the myeloid stem cell. The granulocytic lineage produces neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils, while the monocytic lineage produces monocytes that mature into macrophages and dendritic cells. The myeloid stem cell also gives rise to erythroid and megakaryocytic progenitors. In inflammation, increased myeloid proliferation can produce a left shift with increased precursor forms.

explanation_incorrect.A: The lymphoid stem cell produces B cells, T cells, and NK cells, not granulocytes or monocytes.
explanation_incorrect.B: The common lymphoid progenitor is committed to lymphoid fates only and cannot form granulocytes or monocytes.
explanation_incorrect.D: The erythroid stem cell is committed to red blood cell production only.
explanation_incorrect.E: The megakaryocytic stem cell is committed to platelet production only.

educationalObjective: Granulocytes and monocytes are both derived from the myeloid stem cell.
